sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝，字元真，廆第三子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhen, was Murong Hui’s third son.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was the third son of Murong Hui.

sourceUnits.zh: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
sourceUnits.en: He had a dragon countenance and plaque-like teeth, and stood seven chi eight cun tall.
sourceUnits.literal: Dragon face and “plaque” teeth; body height seven chi eight cun.

sourceUnits.zh: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, resourceful, devoted to the classics, and adept at reading the stars.
sourceUnits.literal: Heroic and resolute, abundant in stratagem; esteemed classical learning; skilled in astronomy.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆為遼東公，立為世子。
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Hui was named duke of Liaodong, Huang was made his heir.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui became Duke of Liaodong, he was established as heir apparent.

sourceUnits.zh: 建武初，拜為冠軍將軍、左賢王，封望平侯，率眾征討，累有功。
sourceUnits.en: Early in the Jianwu era he was named general who champions the army and left worthy prince, created marquis of Wangping, and led troops on several successful expeditions.
sourceUnits.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, appointed General Who Champions the Army, Left Worthy Prince, enfeoffed Marquis of Wangping; led host in campaigns; repeatedly had merit.

sourceUnits.zh: 太甯末，拜平北將軍，進封朝鮮公。
sourceUnits.en: Late in the Taining era he became general who pacifies the north and was promoted to duke of Chaoxian.
sourceUnits.literal: At the end of Taining, appointed General Who Pacifies the North; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Chaoxian.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆卒，嗣位，以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died he succeeded him, serving as general who pacifies the north and acting governor of Pingzhou with authority over the whole command.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, he succeeded the position; as general who pacifies the north acted as governor of Ping Province, supervising and holding the interior of the command.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋而宇文乞得龜為其別部逸豆歸所逐，奔死於外，皝率騎討之，逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。
sourceUnits.en: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon Yuwen Qidegui was by his separate division Yidougui expelled, fled and died outside; Huang led cavalry to campaign against him; Yidougui feared and requested peace; thereupon built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 遼弟蘭與翰寇柳城，都尉石琮擊敗之。
sourceUnits.en: Liao’s younger brother Lan together with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.
sourceUnits.literal: Liao’s younger brother Lan with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝戒汗曰：「賊眾氣銳，難與爭鋒，宜顧萬全，慎勿輕進，必須兵集陣整，然後擊之。」
sourceUnits.en: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is numerous and their spirit keen; it is hard to contend at the spear-tip. You ought to look to complete safety, and carefully do not advance lightly; you must wait until the troops are gathered and the lines set, then strike them.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is many and their spirit sharp; hard to contend edge; ought to look to complete safety, carefully do not lightly advance; must wait until troops are gathered and lines set, then strike them.”

sourceUnits.zh: 汗性驍銳，遣千餘騎為前鋒而進，封弈止之，汗不從，為蘭所敗，死者大半。
sourceUnits.en: Han’s nature was fierce and keen; he dispatched over a thousand cavalry as a vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him, but Han did not follow, was defeated by Lan, and the dead were more than half.
sourceUnits.literal: Han’s nature was fierce and sharp; dispatched over a thousand cavalry as vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him; Han did not follow; was defeated by Lan; dead were more than half.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝以步騎五萬擊之，師次柳城，蘭、歸皆遁。
sourceUnits.en: Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; Lan and Gui both fled when the army halted at Liucheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang with infantry and cavalry fifty thousand struck them; army halted at Liucheng; Lan and Gui both fled.

sourceUnits.zh: 使其世子俊伐段遼諸城，封弈攻宇文別部，皆大捷而歸。
sourceUnits.en: He had his heir apparent Jun campaign against Duan Liao’s cities, and Feng Yi attack a separate Yuwen division; both returned in great victory.
sourceUnits.literal: Made his heir apparent Jun campaign against Duan Liao’s cities; Feng Yi attacked Yuwen’s separate division; both great victory and return.

sourceUnits.zh: 後徙昌黎郡，築好城于乙連東，使將軍蘭勃戍之，以逼乙連。
sourceUnits.en: He later relocated Changli commandery, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and had general Lan Bo garrison it to press Yilian.
sourceUnits.literal: Later moved Changli commandery, built Haocheng east of Yilian, had general Lan Bo garrison it, to press Yilian.

sourceUnits.zh: 以其妻段氏為王后，世子俊為太子，皆如魏武、晉文輔政故事。
sourceUnits.en: He made his wife Lady Duan queen and the heir apparent Jun crown prince, all following the Wei Wu and Jin Wen precedents of assisting in government.
sourceUnits.literal: Made his wife Lady Duan queen, heir apparent Jun crown prince, all like Wei Wu and Jin Wen’s precedent of assisting government.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
sourceUnits.en: Huang was about to plan against the Shi clan; he calmly told the generals: “Shi Hu thinks the cities of Anle and the rest are strictly and heavily guarded, and surely sets no defenses north and south of the city; now if we take a deceitful route and strike where he does not expect, the whole northern territory of Ji can be broken.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang was about to plan the Shi clan; leisurely said to the generals: “Shi Jilong thinks the cities of Anle and the rest guard defense strict and heavy; surely north and south of the city he does not set equipment; now if by deceitful route go out where he does not expect, the whole north of Ji can be broken.”

sourceUnits.zh: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, King of Yan; the rest of offices all as before.

sourceUnits.zh: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
sourceUnits.en: The Four Assistants and the generals shall promptly fix quotas for artisans and merchants; the rest shall return to farming.
sourceUnits.literal: As for the numbers of artisans and merchants, let the Four Assistants and the generals promptly establish the overall quotas; let the remainder return to farming.

sourceUnits.zh: 三年，遣其世子俊與恪率騎萬七千東襲夫餘，克之，虜其王及部眾五萬餘口以還。
sourceUnits.en: In the third year he sent his heir Jun and Ke with seventeen thousand cavalry to raid Puyu eastward; they took it, captured its king and more than fifty thousand of the tribe, and returned.
sourceUnits.literal: In the third year, sent his heir apparent Jun with Ke leading cavalry seventeen thousand east to raid Puyu, took it, captured their king and division host over fifty thousand mouths and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝親臨東庠考試學生，其經通秀異者，擢充近侍。
sourceUnits.en: Huang personally went to the eastern school to examine students; those whose command of the classics was thorough and outstanding were promoted to fill posts as close attendants.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang personally arrived at the eastern school to examine students; those whose classics were thorough and outstanding, promoted to fill close attendance.

sourceUnits.zh: 以勃海人為興集縣，河間人為寧集縣，廣平、魏郡人為興平縣，東萊、北海人為育黎縣，吳人為吳縣，悉隸燕國。
sourceUnits.en: He made the Bohai people into Xingji County, the Hejian people into Ningji County, the Guangping and Wei commandery people into Xingping County, the Donglai and Beihai people into Yuli County, and the Wu people into Wu County, all subordinate to the state of Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Made Bohai people Xingji county, Hejian people Ningji county, Guangping and Wei commandery people Xingping county, Donglai and Beihai people Yuli county, Wu people Wu county—all subordinate to the state of Yan.

sourceUnits.zh: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
sourceUnits.en: He was carried back to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun to entrust him with affairs after his death.
sourceUnits.literal: He returned to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun, entrusting him with affairs after his death.

sourceUnits.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
sourceUnits.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.

sourceUnits.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
sourceUnits.en: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.
sourceUnits.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
sourceUnits.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.
sourceUnits.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
sourceUnits.en: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.
sourceUnits.literal: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。
sourceUnits.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
sourceUnits.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.

sourceUnits.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
sourceUnits.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;
sourceUnits.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;

sourceUnits.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」
sourceUnits.en: if I miss, come on.”
sourceUnits.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”

sourceUnits.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
sourceUnits.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.
sourceUnits.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.

sourceUnits.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
sourceUnits.en: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.
sourceUnits.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
sourceUnits.en: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.
sourceUnits.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.

sourceUnits.zh: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
sourceUnits.en: When Wang Jun held the province, Yu was transferred to administration aide; Jun was jealous and would not employ him.
sourceUnits.literal: Wang Jun held the province, transferred to aide in the bureau of administration, envied yet could not employ him.

sourceUnits.zh: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」
sourceUnits.en: Let both sides remedy their former faults and renew good faith as at the beginning, so the state may have the security of Mount Tai and the common people receive the blessing of laying down their burdens.”
sourceUnits.literal: Wish both pursue former faults, communicate sincerity as at the beginning, cause the state to have Mount Tai’s peace, the black-haired people to receive the favor of resting shoulders.”

sourceUnits.zh: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
sourceUnits.en: Earlier, Lu Chen of Fanyang always praised him, saying, “I have lived through Jin’s clear peace and have broadly observed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise and resolute, steadfast in faith and fierce in righteousness—men like Yang Shilun are in truth few.”
sourceUnits.literal: In the beginning, Fan Yang’s Lu Chen always praised him, saying: “I have reached Jin’s clear peace, broadly viewed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise, resolute, faithful in duty and fierce in righteousness—like Yang Shilun, in truth also not many.”
